organizations.role: Travis County Commissioner, Precinct 3, 2002-08 & 2013-2020; described in press coverage as 'Travis County's last Republican' commissioner
organizations.notes: Zip 78735 matches the Austin home address (1403 Club Ridge Cove) on Gerald T. Daugherty's Texas Ethics Commission lobbyist registration, and occupation 'RETIRED' matches his December 2020 retirement from the Travis County Commissioners Court after 14 years as the county's sole Republican commissioner. He later became a restaurateur (Jack Allen's Kitchen) after decades as owner of Pleasant Valley Sportsplex. FEC/PAC-side searches (Club for Growth, NRA, Republican Party of Texas PAC, etc.) turned up general Republican-donor-space results but no specific PAC-board or PAC-leadership record tied to him personally beyond the existing 250-donation federal giving history already on file.

Brian Rodgers is a long-time Austin real estate investor and civic activist. An Austin Bulldog profile (via search snippet; the page returned 403 when fetched) says he co-founded Rodgers and Reichle Inc. in 1992 with Kevin Reichle and considered a 2010 council run against Randi Shade. In 2015 he settled an open-records lawsuit against the City of Austin for $5,000. His requests had covered the Downtown Austin Alliance's support for the light-rail measure (FOIFT, Nov 2015). He also sued the city and Endeavor over Domain tax rebates (2004 settlement, per search snippet). The employer string and 78703 match the filing. Real-estate principal, but his public record is as a critic of city subsidies, not a developer lobby. FEC check: the FEC API returned HTTP 429 and OpenSecrets refused the fetch, so PAC recipients of his roughly 218 federal donations (from the input) were not reviewed and fec_pac is false. TX lobbyist check: site searches found nothing. The 2012 TEC list (read in full) has only an unrelated Kelly S. Rodgers. The 2026 TEC PDF could not be parsed. Israel/Palestine (both sides), oil/gas, gun and defense searches found nothing. The bio page (Austin Bulldog) could not be fully read (403), so bio_full_read is false.

FEC Schedule A records list Kirk Mitchell, Rollingwood TX 78746, occupation 'Securities Investment', employer 'Self', matching the filing. The ~200 records reviewed (2024-2026) are small-dollar ActBlue-earmarked gifts to Democratic candidates (Harris, Ocasio-Cortez, Sanders, Jasmine for Texas, Allred, Sherrod Brown, Tester, Casey, Osborn, Vindman, Kunce, etc.) plus Blue to the Future. No AIPAC/UDP, J Street, gun, oil & gas or defense PACs appeared in the records read (not every one of the 164 records was reviewed). No TEC lobbyist registration. No bio/LinkedIn found.

William 'Bill' Bunch co-founded the SOS Alliance in 1992 and has been its Executive Director since 2000. He is an environmental attorney; his Justia profile lists William Gene Bunch with SOS Alliance as his affiliation. This matches the donor's occupation ('Attorney') and employer ('SOS Alliance'). Federal contributor records could not be checked (FEC API 429, OpenSecrets blocked, fec.gov renders client-side); web searches pairing his name with PAC terms found nothing. The TEC check by site-restricted web search found no lobbyist registration. The full bios on Travis Audubon and the SOS About page were read. No Israel/Palestine, oil/gas, gun or defense ties were found.
